mainTopic: The source for the ban on offering a very young animal, and whether אותו ואת בנו and its מלקות apply to קדשים according to רבי שמעון
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining that offering an animal younger than eight days is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה. That counts as a positive commandment, so there are no lashes. It asks how 'from the eighth day' can be the source, since רבי אפטוריקי needs that verse to teach that the night before the eighth day is for making the animal holy and the day is for offering it. The answer is that another verse in שמות teaches the positive commandment. Then רב המנונא reports that, for רבי שמעון, אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים, because slaughtering קדשים does not make the meat permitted. רבא challenges this from a ברייתא about mother-and-young offerings slaughtered outside the עזרה. He first fixes the ברייתא by showing words are missing. Its last case, where רבי שמעון gives only a לאו, proves that the איסור does apply to קדשים. So רבא re-reads רב המנונא: only the מלקות does not apply, because the warning is a הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק. רבא's rulings about a חולין mother with a שלמים or עולה offspring follow the same idea.

steps.title: The Torah turned this prohibition into a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the ban on offering a very young animal was changed by the Torah into a positive-commandment type of prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The Torah] turned it into a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that began just before this point. Offering an animal less than eight days old is different, because the Torah turned its prohibition into a positive commandment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other unfit animals fall under a regular לאו ('it shall not be accepted'), which can bring lashes. For an animal too young to be offered, the Torah moved the prohibition into the category of a positive commandment. That is why the usual punishment does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah 'moved it over' into a positive commandment instead of a regular לאו
A positive commandment

phrases.english: [The Torah] transferred it to a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ban on offering an animal less than eight days old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to an earlier question about why offering a very young animal is treated differently
steps.terutzResolutionType: Category distinction: this prohibition is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, not a standard לאו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offering a very young animal should be a regular לאו like the other disqualifications
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah placed it in the positive-commandment category

steps.title: The source: 'From the eighth day and on it will be accepted'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the point from the פסוק 'from the eighth day and on': the eighth day is allowed, and earlier is not. A ban that comes out of a positive statement counts as a positive commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the verse says: 'From the eighth day and onward it will be accepted.' From the eighth day, yes; before that, no. A prohibition that comes out of a positive statement counts as a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn this, and it shows the source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says in a positive way that from day eight the animal is accepted. The ban on earlier days is only implied. A ban that is only implied from a positive statement is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, and it has the status of a positive commandment.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason / what is the source?
It will be accepted (as an offering)
A prohibition that is only implied from a positive statement; it has the status of a positive commandment
Before that, earlier

steps.whyThisMatters: This category explains why someone who offers an animal younger than eight days does not get lashes.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
For the verse says:
'From the eighth day and onward it will be accepted'
from the eighth day, yes;
before that, no.
A prohibition that comes from a positive statement
is [treated as] a positive commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse that supports step 1
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on offering a very young animal is a positive-commandment type of prohibition

steps.title: That verse is already needed for רבי אפטוריקי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source: רבי אפטוריקי already uses 'from the eighth day' to settle a contradiction about the night before the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for what רבי אפטוריקי taught! רבי אפטוריקי pointed out a contradiction. It says 'it shall be seven days with its mother', so on the night after day seven it should already be fit. But it also says 'from the eighth day and onward it will be accepted', so from the eighth day, yes, but on that night, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 2. It says the same פסוק is already being used for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is 'busy' teaching one thing is usually not used to teach a second thing as well. רבי אפטוריקי needs the words 'from the eighth day' to deal with the night before the eighth day. So the words may not be free to teach that this is a positive commandment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
He pointed out a contradiction
With its mother
Is fit

phrases.english: But it is needed
for the teaching of רבי אפטוריקי,
for רבי אפטוריקי pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: 'It shall be seven days with its mother',
which implies that the night [after the seventh day] is fit,
and it is written: 'From the eighth day and onward it will be accepted'
from the eighth day and onward, yes;
the night, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the verse used as proof in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'מיום השמיני והלאה ירצה' as the source for the positive commandment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is already used for רבי אפטוריקי's teaching, so it cannot also be the source here

steps.title: רבי אפטוריקי's solution: the night is for making it holy, the day is for offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אפטוריקי settles his own contradiction. The night before the eighth day is fit for making the animal holy, and the eighth day itself is when it can be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can this be? The night is for making it holy; the day is for having it accepted [as an offering].
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי אפטוריקי's teaching by showing how he settles the contradiction. It completes the challenge, because it shows what the words 'from the eighth day' are being used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק is talking about a different stage. 'Seven days with its mother' allows the animal to be made holy on the night after day seven. 'From the eighth day' teaches that the animal can only be offered on the altar from the eighth day itself. Because the words are used this way, the challenge in step 3 is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: How can these fit together?
Making the animal holy, setting it aside as an offering
Being accepted, actually offered on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's answer to the challenge. It is still part of רבי אפטוריקי's teaching, and it shows why he needs the verse. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: How so?
The night is for consecration,
the day is for acceptance [as an offering].

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? לַיְלָה לִקְדוּשָּׁה, יוֹם לְהַרְצָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אפטוריקי's teaching by giving his resolution
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verse refers to a different stage: making the animal holy versus offering it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses contradict each other about the night after day seven
steps.terutzMaskana: The night is fit for making it holy, and the eighth day is for offering it

steps.title: Another verse teaches the positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a different פסוק in שמות, 'so shall you do with your ox and your sheep', is the source of the positive commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another verse is written: 'So shall you do with your ox and with your sheep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 3. A second פסוק teaches the positive commandment, so the verse in ויקרא is free for רבי אפטוריקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in שמות goes on to say 'on the eighth day you shall give it to Me'. That is a positive command about when to offer the animal. So we still have a positive-commandment source, and it does not clash with רבי אפטוריקי's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Another verse
Your ox
Your sheep / flock

steps.whatToRemember: Offering an animal younger than eight days is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which is treated as a positive commandment. Its source is the verse in שמות, while the verse in ויקרא is used for רבי אפטוריקי's teaching about night versus day.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
'So shall you do with your ox and with your sheep.'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:29. The rest of the פסוק says 'on the eighth day you shall give it to Me'. That's the positive command.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only source is the verse in ויקרא, which is already in use
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse in שמות provides the positive commandment

steps.title: רבי שמעון: אותו ואת בנו does not apply to sacrificial animals
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא reports that רבי שמעון held that the ban on slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day does not apply to קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: רבי שמעון used to say: the law of 'it and its young' does not apply to sacrificial animals.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins here. רב המנונא reports a ruling of רבי שמעון about אותו ואת בנו and sacrificial animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the Torah forbids slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day. רבי שמעון says this ban does not apply when the animals are קדשים. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day
Applies
Sacrificial animals

phrases.english: רב המנונא said:
רבי שמעון used to say:
[The law of] 'it and its young' does not
apply to sacrificial animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the very young animal ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים

steps.title: The reason: slaughtering a sacrificial animal is a slaughter that is not fit
steps.stepSummary: The reason is based on רבי שמעון's rule that a slaughter which does not make the meat permitted does not count as שחיטה. Slaughtering קדשים is that kind of slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since רבי שמעון says that a slaughter that is not fit is not called slaughter, slaughtering a sacrificial animal is also a slaughter that is not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's ruling by linking it to another rule of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a שחיטה only counts if it makes the meat permitted right away. When a sacrificial animal is slaughtered, the meat is not yet permitted until the blood is put on the altar. So that slaughter does not count, and אותו ואת בנו does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted
It is not called (halachic) slaughter
Slaughtering sacrificial animals

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how רבי שמעון's general rule about what counts as שחיטה shapes his rulings in specific cases.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since רבי שמעון says:
a slaughter that is not fit
is not called slaughter,
phrases.notes: 'Not fit' means the slaughter does not make the meat permitted to eat.

phrases.english: slaughtering sacrificial animals also
is a slaughter that is not fit.
phrases.notes: The meat is not permitted until the blood is put on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי שמעון holds that אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted does not count as שחיטה, and slaughtering קדשים is such a slaughter

steps.title: רבא challenges רב המנונא from a ברייתא about sacrifices slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון says that someone who slaughters the second animal of a mother-and-young pair of קדשים outside the עזרה violates only a לאו. This suggests the second animal is disqualified because of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: If a mother and its young, both sacrificial animals, were slaughtered outside the Temple, רבי שמעון says the second one is only under a prohibition. This is because רבי שמעון held that any offering that will be fit later on carries a prohibition but no כרת. The חכמים say that anything with no כרת has no prohibition either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב המנונא's report that, for רבי שמעון, אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the second animal is 'fit to come later' (tomorrow) but not today. The only thing that would block it today is אותו ואת בנו. So the ban seems to apply to קדשים even for רבי שמעון, which contradicts רב המנונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard
A negative commandment (a לאו), usually punished with lashes
Spiritual 'cutting off,' the punishment for slaughtering a valid offering outside
Fit to be offered later, but not yet fit now

steps.confusionAlert: The 'second' animal is not disqualified forever. It is only blocked for today, which is why רבי שמעון calls it 'fit to come after some time.'

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
Itself and its offspring, sacrificial animals, slaughtered outside —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שֵׁנִי בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: for the second, he is under a prohibition,
for Rabbi Shimon would say:
Any offering that is fit to come after some time —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: one who slaughters it outside is under a prohibition, but there is no karet,
and the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת – אֵינוֹ בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: anything that has no karet is not under a prohibition either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's report (steps 6-7) with a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that for רבי שמעון אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the second animal as blocked today, which can only be because of אותו ואת בנו, so the ban applies to קדשים.

steps.title: The baraita does not fit רבי שמעון's own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא was already hard to understand. By רבי שמעון's rule, the first slaughter is not a real שחיטה, so the second animal should still be fit and should carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this was difficult for us: sacrificial animals outside, and the second is only under a prohibition? The first was just 'killed,' so the second could still be accepted on the altar. He should be liable to כרת too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem inside the ברייתא itself. Read the way it is written, it does not fit רבי שמעון's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, a slaughter that does not make the meat permitted is not called שחיטה (step 7). Slaughtering קדשים outside is that kind of slaughter, so the first animal was only 'killed.' Then אותו ואת בנו never kicks in, the second animal stays fully fit, and slaughtering it outside should bring כרת, not just a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult for us (a problem we already had)
He merely killed it (not a real שחיטה)
Would be accepted inside, meaning fit for the altar

phrases.english: And it is difficult for us:
Sacrificial animals outside, and the second is only under a prohibition?
The first — he merely killed it,
phrases.notes: This uses רבי שמעון's rule from step 7: a slaughter that doesn't permit the meat isn't real שחיטה.

phrases.english: the second is one that would be accepted inside,
so let him be liable to karet as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא quoted in step 8 contradicts רבי שמעון's own rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא, which gives רבי שמעון only a לאו for the second animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first slaughter is not שחיטה, the second animal is fully valid, so slaughtering it outside should carry כרת.

steps.title: Words are missing from the ברייתא: the view of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or an unnamed voice) says the ברייתא is missing words. In the full version, according to the רבנן, the first animal brings כרת, and the second is disqualified and exempt from the לאו of slaughtering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it without a name: the ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it teaches. If both sacrificial animals were slaughtered outside, according to the רבנן the first brings כרת, and the second is disqualified and exempt from the prohibition of slaughtering outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא by explaining that some words are missing. It starts by laying out the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the first slaughter counts as שחיטה, so אותו ואת בנו disqualifies the second animal for today. A disqualified animal has no כרת, and by their rule 'no כרת means no לאו,' so there is no punishment at all for slaughtering it outside. The idea of the second animal being disqualified now belongs to the רבנן, not to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words
Without a name (said with no named author)
Disqualified as an offering
The prohibition of slaughtering offerings outside the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן are lenient about slaughtering outside in general. The second animal is exempt only because it is already disqualified today.

phrases.english: And Rava said, and some say it without a name:
The baraita is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
Sacrificial animals, both of them slaughtered outside —
according to the Rabbis, the first is punishable by karet,
the second is disqualified
and exempt from the prohibition of slaughtering outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 9 by restoring missing words in the ברייתא; רבא's objection from step 8 is then pressed against the corrected ברייתא in steps 13-14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to have רבי שמעון disqualify the second animal because of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The disqualification of the second animal is the view of the רבנן, who hold that the first slaughter counts.

steps.title: In the corrected ברייתא, רבי שמעון gives כרת for both animals
steps.stepSummary: In the corrected ברייתא, רבי שמעון holds that both animals carry כרת. Since the first slaughter does not count, the second animal is never disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, both of them are punishable by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The corrected ברייתא finishes with רבי שמעון's view: someone who slaughters either animal outside gets כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, a slaughter outside does not permit the meat, so it is not real שחיטה, and אותו ואת בנו never blocks the second animal. So the second animal is a valid offering, and slaughtering it outside brings full כרת. This removes the difficulty of step 9, but רבא's challenge to רב המנונא is not yet settled. It comes back in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishable (plural)
Both of them
A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted, which רבי שמעון says is not שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: In the corrected ברייתא, when both are slaughtered outside: for רבי שמעון the first slaughter is not real שחיטה, so both animals bring כרת. For the רבנן, the first brings כרת and the second is disqualified with no punishment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one rule, 'a slaughter that doesn't permit the meat is not שחיטה,' decides the outcome, and it sets up the remaining cases that רבא will use against רב המנונא.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, both of them are punishable by karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the corrected ברייתא begun in step 10 with רבי שמעון's view
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי שמעון, slaughtering both animals outside brings כרת, because the first slaughter outside is not real שחיטה.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: first animal outside, second inside
steps.stepSummary: The corrected ברייתא gives the case where the mother is slaughtered outside the עזרה and the young inside. The רבנן and רבי שמעון disagree about the second animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first is slaughtered outside and the second inside: according to the רבנן, the first brings כרת, and the second is disqualified but the slaughterer is exempt. According to רבי שמעון, the second is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the corrected ברייתא. This is a new case: the first animal is slaughtered outside and the second inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the first slaughter counts, so the second animal becomes 'too early' and is unfit. Since it was slaughtered inside, he is exempt from the punishment for slaughtering outside. For רבי שמעון, slaughtering קדשים outside is not a real שחיטה, so the second animal is not affected and is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the עזרה (Temple courtyard)
Inside the עזרה
Punishable by כרת
Disqualified for the מזבח, but the slaughterer is not punished
Fit to be brought on the מזבח

phrases.english: One outside and one inside:
according to the Rabbis, the first is punishable by karet,
the second is disqualified and he is exempt;
according to Rabbi Shimon, the second is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the corrected ברייתא from steps 10-11 with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: first gets כרת, second is unfit and exempt. רבי שמעון: second is fit, because the slaughter outside does not count.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: first animal inside, second outside
steps.stepSummary: The last case of the ברייתא: the first animal is slaughtered inside and the second outside. רבי שמעון says the second brings only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first is slaughtered inside and the second outside: according to the רבנן, the first is fit and he is exempt, and the second is unfit and he is exempt. According to רבי שמעון, the second brings a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last case of the ברייתא. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the first is a normal קרבן. The second is 'too early,' so it could not be brought inside, and that is why he is exempt for slaughtering it outside. רבי שמעון says the second brings only a לאו, the rule for an animal that is 'too early' and slaughtered outside. That means he holds the first slaughter inside did make the second animal 'too early.'

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment (לאו), lighter than כרת
An animal whose time has not yet come; it is 'too early' to be offered

phrases.english: One inside and one outside:
according to the Rabbis, the first is fit and he is exempt,
the second is unfit and he is exempt,
according to Rabbi Shimon, the second is under a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case of step 12 and supplies the detail רבא will use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: first fit, second unfit, exempt both times. רבי שמעון: the second slaughtered outside brings only a לאו.

steps.title: If אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים, why only a לאו?
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains his challenge to רב המנונא. רבי שמעון's ruling in the last case only makes sense if אותו ואת בנו does apply to קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים, why is the second animal only a לאו and nothing more? He should also get כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the challenge against רב המנונא is spelled out, using the last case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אותו ואת בנו did not apply to קדשים, the second animal would be a perfectly fit קרבן. Slaughtering a fit קרבן outside brings כרת. Since רבי שמעון says it is only a לאו, the second animal must be unfit because of אותו ואת בנו, so the איסור does apply to קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind; if you think that...
And nothing more
Let him be liable

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the first slaughter inside automatically counts. By רב המנונא's reason (step 7), even a slaughter inside does not permit the meat until the blood is sprinkled, so it would not count, the second animal would be fully fit, and slaughtering it outside should bring כרת. Since רבי שמעון gives only a לאו, the first slaughter must count for אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that 'itself and its offspring' does not apply to sacrificial animals,

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי אַמַּאי בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וְתוּ לָא?
phrases.english: why is the second only under a prohibition and nothing more?
Let him be liable to karet as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of step 13 to attack רב המנונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's statement that אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A לאו and not כרת means the second animal was unfit. The only reason it could be unfit is אותו ואת בנו, so the איסור must apply to קדשים.

steps.title: רבא re-reads רב המנונא: only the lashes do not apply
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes how we understand רב המנונא. The איסור of אותו ואת בנו does apply to קדשים, but the punishment of מלקות does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what רב המנונא means: the lashes of אותו ואת בנו do not apply to קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the first reading of רב המנונא and gives a new one that fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we thought רב המנונא meant the whole איסור does not apply to קדשים, and the ברייתא disproved that. Now רבא says the איסור does apply, so the second animal is really unfit. רב המנונא only meant that one does not get מלקות for it with קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier idea for a new one
This is what he means; a re-reading of a statement
Lashes, the punishment for breaking a לאו

steps.whatToRemember: After the challenge, רב המנונא's rule is narrowed: אותו ואת בנו applies to קדשים, but there are no מלקות for it there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between the איסור itself and the punishment for it. The rule can stay in place even when the מלקות does not.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said,
this is what Rav Hamnuna is saying:
the lashes of 'itself and its offspring'
do not apply to sacrificial animals,
phrases.notes: The word אֵין ('not') from the row before belongs here in English.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי קָא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by narrowing רב המנונא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the statement (הכי קאמר): it is narrowed from the איסור to the punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב המנונא meant the איסור of אותו ואת בנו does not apply to קדשים at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור applies to קדשים; only the מלקות does not.

steps.title: Why there is no מלקות: the warning is uncertain
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why קדשים bring no מלקות for אותו ואת בנו. Until the blood is sprinkled the meat is not permitted, so the warning at the time of slaughter is uncertain, and an uncertain warning does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as the blood has not been sprinkled, the meat is not permitted. So at the moment he slaughters, the warning is an uncertain warning, and an uncertain warning is not considered a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבא's answer in Step 15: why the איסור applies to קדשים but the punishment of מלקות does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן's meat only becomes permitted after the blood is sprinkled. When the second animal is slaughtered, nobody knows yet whether that will happen, so nobody knows whether he is really breaking the איסור. A warning given in that state of doubt is a הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק, and it cannot make him liable for מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח, which makes the meat permitted
The warning given just before a sin, which is required before מלקות
An uncertain warning, given when it is not yet clear whether the act will turn out to be a sin

steps.whatToRemember: With קדשים the איסור of אותו ואת בנו applies, but there is no מלקות. The reason is that the warning is a הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק, which does not count as a warning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns רב המנונא's rule into a general idea, הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק לֹא שְׁמָהּ הַתְרָאָה. The next steps use that idea to explain רבא's other rulings.

phrases.english: Since as long as he has not sprinkled the blood,
the meat is not permitted,
then from the moment that he slaughters,
it is an uncertain warning,
and an uncertain warning is not considered a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind Step 15's claim that the איסור applies to קדשים but מלקות does not.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason: the warning is uncertain because the meat may never become permitted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the איסור applies to קדשים, we might have thought it should bring מלקות just like חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: No מלקות, because at the time of slaughter the warning is a הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק, which does not count.

steps.title: רבא's case of a חולין mother and a שלמים offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows רבא holds this idea elsewhere. If the mother is חולין and the offspring is a שלמים, slaughtering the חולין first and the שלמים second makes him פטור. Slaughtering the שלמים first and the חולין second makes him חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא is consistent with his own reasoning, as he said: if the mother is חולין and her offspring is a שלמים, and he slaughtered the חולין and then the שלמים, he is exempt. If he slaughtered the שלמים and then the חולין, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of רבא to show that he consistently uses the idea of הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the שלמים is slaughtered second, it is the act being warned about, and its meat may never become permitted, so the warning is uncertain and he is פטור. When the חולין is slaughtered second, it is a regular חולין slaughter with nothing uncertain about it, so the warning is solid and he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning; the ruling fits his opinion elsewhere
A regular animal that is not consecrated
A peace offering, whose meat is eaten after the blood is sprinkled
Exempt (here, from מלקות)
Liable (here, to מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: What matters is which animal is slaughtered SECOND, because the second slaughter is the one that breaks אותו ואת בנו. Only if the second animal is the קרבן is the warning uncertain.

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
If she is non-sacred and her offspring is a peace offering,
and he slaughtered the non-sacred one
and afterward slaughtered the peace offering, he is exempt.
But if he slaughtered the peace offering and afterward the non-sacred one, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק idea from Step 16 is also behind another ruling of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mother חולין, offspring שלמים: חולין first and then שלמים means פטור; שלמים first and then חולין means חייב.

steps.title: רבא opens a new case: an offspring brought as an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a new ruling about a mother that is חולין and an offspring brought as an עולה. He starts with the obvious part: slaughtering the חולין first and then the עולה is certainly פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: if the mother is חולין and her offspring is an עולה, it is not necessary to say that if he slaughtered the חולין and then the עולה, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבא first states the obvious half of the עולה case, and his real new point (the other order) comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order חולין first and then עולה works the same as the שלמים case: the קרבן is slaughtered second, the warning is uncertain, and he is פטור. The words לָא מִיבַּעְיָא tell us this half is obvious, and that the surprising ruling is still coming.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
It is not necessary to say; it is obvious (a hint that a bigger point is coming)

steps.confusionAlert: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא is not the ruling's main point. It is the easy half, and the real new point, the opposite order, follows next.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If she is non-sacred and her offspring is a burnt offering,
it is not necessary to say

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט חוּלִּין וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט עוֹלָה דְּפָטוּר,
phrases.english: that if he slaughtered the non-sacred one and afterward slaughtered the burnt offering, he is exempt,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הִיא חוּלִּין וּבְנָהּ עוֹלָה, לָא מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שלמים case in Step 17 to a parallel case with an עולה, starting with the obvious half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mother חולין, offspring עולה: slaughtering the חולין first and then the עולה is obviously פטור (the bigger point follows).
